Donor-π-Acceptor push-pull organic molecules and their versatile applications

Abstract:

Donor&ndash&pi&ndashacceptor (D&ndash&pi&ndashA) push&ndashpull organic chromophores are molecular systems comprising an electron-donating unit and an electron-accepting unit connected through a &pi-conjugated bridge. The presence of these electronically distinct groups imparts an intrinsic dipolar character to the molecules, resulting in unique photophysical and electronic properties. Owing to their tunable optical behavior, environmental sensitivity, and, in many cases, good aqueous solubility, D&ndash&pi&ndashA chromophores have found widespread applications as molecular probes in fluorescence imaging, molecular recognition, and chemical sensing. In recent years, D&ndash&pi&ndashA chromophores exhibiting solid-state fluorescence have attracted considerable attention because of their promising applications in organic electronics, solid-state lighting, optoelectronic devices, sensors, and anti-counterfeiting technologies. Their ability to retain efficient emission in the aggregated and solid states makes them particularly valuable for the development of advanced functional materials. Although a large number of D&ndash&pi&ndashA molecules have been reported in the literature, a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between molecular structure and photophysical properties remains elusive. In the present research program, a series of novel D&ndash&pi&ndashA luminophores will be designed and synthesized. Their photophysical characteristics will be systematically investigated with particular emphasis on establishing detailed structure&ndashproperty relationships. Furthermore, the potential applications of these luminophores in organic electronics, solid-state lighting, chemosensing, and bioimaging will be explored.
